subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — Liability Cap Proposal
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecloud.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial MSA redlines — liability cap

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Alicia and I reviewed the liability section and we have a couple of high-level concerns around the proposed cap. Acme’s procurement requires a commercially reasonable cap tied to fees paid, and we typically request a multiple of the annual fees rather than an aggregate lifetime cap for multi-year agreements.

In particular:
- We prefer cap = greater of $500k or 3x annual fees (to align with our risk exposure per year).
- We ask for a carve-out for breaches of confidentiality / data protection with a higher cap (or unlimited liability for indemnities tied to data breaches).
- Exclude consequential damages carve-outs for both parties but keep direct damages limited as above.

Can you confirm Redwood’s flexibility here? Alicia is on copy and can take the legal redlines if we progress. We have a target signature before end of November.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Strategic Sourcing
Acme Cloud Platform

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — liability cap

Daniel —

Appreciate the quick read. We want to be cooperative here and avoid a protracted back-and-forth on core commercials — happy to propose an alternative that meets Acme’s concern around per-year exposure while keeping Redwood’s exposure predictable for enterprise customers.

Internal ask: Marissa / Karthik, does Redwood have precedent for a per-year multiple vs. aggregate lifetime cap in enterprise deals? Also, do we have a firm internal threshold for data breach carve-outs?

My thinking (proposal to send to Acme):
- Liability cap = greater of $250,000 or 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months (measured on an annualized basis).
- For data breaches causing unauthorized access to customer data, cap = greater of $1,000,000 or 3x fees paid in prior 12 months.
- Standard carve-outs for IP infringement and willful misconduct remain (no cap).
- Mutual exclusion of consequential damages preserved.

I can send this proposal to Alicia if you all are aligned.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — liability cap

Jordan / Karthik —

Precedent notes from legal: we commonly do a multiple of annual fees (1x–3x) depending on ARR and strategic posture. For net-new mid-market customers we default to 1x; for enterprise strategic deals we have flexibility to 2x. Data breach carve-outs: Legal prefers a higher cap rather than unlimited liability — typical is $1M or 3x annual fees for security-related claims.

Also flag: Finance needs to confirm whether a $250k minimum floor is acceptable for revenue recognition and risk provisioning. If Acme pushes 3x and has $2M annual spend, Redwood exposure could materially exceed our internal risk band without a commensurate change in pricing or indemnity language.

Recommend sending Jordan’s proposal as a starting point and let Acme respond. If they insist on 3x annually we escalate to Rishi for approval.

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmecloud.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 08:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — liability cap

Alicia / Daniel —

Thanks for the redlines. Per our internal review we can move on this basis:

Proposed compromise (Redwood):
- Liability cap: greater of $250,000 or 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months (annualized).
- Security/Data breach carve-out: greater of $1,000,000 or 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months for claims arising from unauthorized access to Customer Data.
- IP indemnity and willful misconduct: uncapped (standard carve-outs).
- Mutual exclusion of consequential damages remains.

Rationale: this gives Acme a year-by-year alignment while keeping Redwood’s total exposure bounded and consistent with other enterprise agreements. If Acme provides an annual spend projection, we can compute the numeric exposure for finance to review.

I’ve attached a redlined version of the MSA and the Order Form with the proposed language. Please review and let us know if the team can accept.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmecloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — liability cap

Jordan —

Thanks for the proposal and for surfacing the finance risk considerations. From Acme Legal’s perspective we remain concerned the proposal understates Acme’s programmatic exposure over longer multi-year arrangements. Our counter-proposal is:

- Liability cap: greater of $500,000 or 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months, with a sunset review at year 2 (i.e., if the relationship continues we re-evaluate based on actual spend).
- Security/Data breach carve-out: uncapped for regulatory fines and third-party claims where Redwood’s negligence caused the breach; otherwise 4x fees paid in prior 12 months for remediation costs (we can provide specific scenarios).

We understand Redwood wants predictability. Can you escalate to Rishi if Redwood cannot accept 3x? If we can get a numeric example of 2x vs 3x exposure for Acme’s forecasted spend it would help procurement sign-off.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Acme Cloud Platform

--

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmecloud.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — liability cap (Escalation)

Alicia / Jordan / team —

Thanks for the clear framing. I reviewed the terms and Redwood’s appetite here: we are prepared to move from 2x to 2.5x of prior 12 months fees with the following guardrails:

- Cap: greater of $350,000 or 2.5x fees paid in prior 12 months.
- Security breach: greater of $1,500,000 or 4x fees paid in prior 12 months for remediation and third-party claims, but regulatory fines remain subject to applicable law and insurance (we cannot accept uncapped regulatory fines).
- Maintain IP and willful misconduct carve-outs.
- Include a 24-month review clause to revisit the cap if spend materially increases.

If Acme can accept 2.5x, we can update the redline and route for signature this week. Otherwise Jordan, please advise next steps — I can authorize up to 3x only with a revenue uplift / price adjustment.

-Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
